explanation: Used to introduce a surprising or newly discovered fact. 'It turns out' signals that reality is different from what was expected or believed.
explanationKo: 놀랍거나 새로 발견된 사실을 소개할 때 사용합니다. 'It turns out'은 현실이 예상이나 믿음과 다르다는 것을 나타냅니다.
examples: And it turns out that nothing could be farther from the truth.
It turns out that even when you're at rest and thinking of nothing, your brain is highly active.
It turns out to be very difficult to help the brain recover from stroke.

explanation: Used to introduce or define a technical term or concept by renaming it in simpler or more formal terms. Common in academic and explanatory speaking.
explanationKo: 기술 용어나 개념을 더 간단하거나 공식적인 용어로 재명명하여 소개하거나 정의할 때 사용합니다. 학술적이고 설명적인 말하기에서 흔합니다.
examples: It's something we call neuroplasticity.
Between brain cells, what we call neurons.
So there are certain characteristics of brain structure and function that we call biomarkers.

pattern: The more/increased X, the more Y (Comparative Correlation)
explanation: Expresses a proportional relationship where an increase in one factor leads to an increase in another. Often used to emphasize cause and effect.
explanationKo: 한 요소의 증가가 다른 요소의 증가로 이어지는 비례 관계를 표현합니다. 인과 관계를 강조할 때 자주 사용됩니다.
examples: Increased difficulty, increased struggle, if you will, during practice actually leads to both more learning and greater structural change in the brain.

explanation: Questions posed not to elicit answers but to engage the audience and introduce a new topic. Very common in TED talks and public speaking.
explanationKo: 답을 이끌어내기 위해서가 아니라 청중의 관심을 끌고 새로운 주제를 소개하기 위해 던지는 질문입니다. TED 강연과 대중 연설에서 매우 흔합니다.
examples: So how do we learn? And why do some of us learn things more easily than others?
Why do our kids sometimes fail in school?
And why don't people fully recover from brain damage?

pattern: Not only A but also B (Additive Emphasis)
explanation: Used to add a second, often more surprising or important point to the first. Creates emphasis by pairing two ideas together.
explanationKo: 첫 번째 포인트에 두 번째, 종종 더 놀랍거나 중요한 포인트를 추가할 때 사용합니다. 두 가지 아이디어를 짝지어 강조를 만듭니다.
examples: It's being shaped both structurally and functionally by everything you do, but also by everything that you don't do.
The uniqueness of your brain will affect you, both as a learner and also as a teacher.

explanation: The present perfect tense is used to describe research findings that remain relevant to the present. Common in academic discourse to connect past discoveries with current understanding.
explanationKo: 현재와 관련이 있는 연구 결과를 설명할 때 현재완료 시제를 사용합니다. 학술적 담론에서 과거의 발견을 현재의 이해와 연결할 때 흔합니다.
examples: What we know about the brain is changing at a breathtaking pace.
And research from my group actually shows that the health-related quality of life of Canadians with stroke has declined.
By studying the brain after stroke, we've learned a lot.

explanation: The passive voice shifts focus from the agent to the action or result, which is typical in scientific discourse to maintain objectivity.
explanationKo: 수동태는 행위자에서 행위나 결과로 초점을 옮기며, 객관성을 유지하기 위해 과학적 담론에서 일반적입니다.
examples: These changes are not limited by age.
Medical intervention studies are specifically designed to minimize variability.
Your plastic brain is constantly being shaped by the world around you.

explanation: Uses 'if' clauses to set up conditions for discussing brain-related scenarios, often mixing real and hypothetical conditions in academic speaking.
explanationKo: 뇌 관련 시나리오를 논의하기 위한 조건을 설정할 때 'if' 절을 사용하며, 학술적 말하기에서 현실적 조건과 가정적 조건을 혼합하는 경우가 많습니다.
examples: Which is on the left side of your brain, if you're right-handed, is larger than the other side.
So for you, learning music may come very easily, but learning to snowboard, much harder.

pattern: Discourse Markers for Structure (So, Now, And)
explanation: Words like 'so', 'now', and 'and' at the beginning of sentences serve as discourse markers to signal transitions between topics, add new information, or draw conclusions.
explanationKo: 'so', 'now', 'and'와 같은 단어들이 문장 시작에서 담화 표지로 사용되어 주제 간 전환, 새 정보 추가, 또는 결론 도출을 나타냅니다.
examples: So brain research is one of the great frontiers.
Now, some of these misconceptions are more obvious than others.
And perhaps the most exciting, the most interesting and transformative.

explanation: Direct commands used at the end of the talk to motivate the audience to take action. Creates urgency and personal engagement.
explanationKo: 강연 끝에서 청중에게 행동을 촉구하기 위해 사용하는 직접 명령문입니다. 긴급감과 개인적 참여를 만듭니다.
examples: Study how and what you learn best.
Repeat those behaviors that are healthy for your brain and break those behaviors and habits that are not.
Go out and build the brain you want.

explanation: A cleft sentence splits a simple clause to emphasize one particular element, bringing focus to key information.
explanationKo: 분열문(cleft sentence)은 단순 절을 나누어 특정 요소를 강조하며, 핵심 정보에 초점을 맞춥니다.
examples: That is, what is it that limits and facilitates neuroplasticity?
It's these physical changes that are now going to support long-term memories.

explanation: Modal verbs and hedging expressions soften claims and avoid absolute statements, which is a key feature of academic English.
explanationKo: 조동사와 완화 표현은 주장을 부드럽게 하고 절대적 진술을 피하며, 이는 학술 영어의 핵심 특징입니다.
examples: For some of us, it's going to take a lot more practice and for others it may take far less.
As we age, do we tend to forget things?
Learning music may come very easily, but learning to snowboard, much harder.
